unite_adi: REGULAR UPPER SECONDARY-YEAR 10-LEVEL: B1.2 THEME 2: CLASSROOM LIFE & LEARNING

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students create a project titled "Classroom Life and Learning," focusing on three main components: learning activities in the classroom, personal learning styles, and learning with technology. Students will begin by describing the different types of activities they participate in during lessons, such as group discussions, individual assignments, or hands-on experiments, and explain how these activities help them learn. They then reflect on their personal learning styles-whether they learn best by listening, seeing, or doing—and provide examples of strategies or techniques that work for them. Finally, students explore the role of technology in their classroom learning, discussing tools like smart boards, tablets, or online resources, and how these enhance their education. The project can include written explanations, drawings, or digital presentations to make it creative and engaging. Students present their work in class, and the assignment will be evaluated based on clarity, creativity, content, and presentation skills. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''classroom life and learning with its components such as learning activities in the classroom; personal learning styles; learning with technology in the classroom'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student of an upper secondary school in year 10 may know what classroom life and learning, learning styles, roles and responsibilities, activities and events at school mean in their own language as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in another language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students of an upper secondary school in year 10, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''classroom life and learning'' in English from previous themes and/or years such as ''to study, to learn, homework, and so on'' and also some structures such as ''What kind of schools are there? What are they? What do students regularly do at schools? How do they feel in their schools?'' in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in an upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''classroom life and learning with its components such as learning activities in the classroom; personal learning styles; learning with technology in the classroom'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a contextual classroom poster could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss about the poster in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To talk about learning activities in the classroom and learning with technology in the classroom in English through a drama technique by using target vocabulary. Activity 1: Classroom Drama Box The teacher prepares classroom situations, such as forgetting an assignment, asking for help, or explaining how to use a laptop, and gives each group a different scenario. Students work in pairs or small groups to create a short dialogue using target vocabulary (e.g., assignments, brainstorming, analyses) and grammar (e.g., modal verbs, reflexive pronouns). They act out their dialogue in front of the class, using expressions like ''Can I explain something?'' or ''I’ll summarise the main points''. After each role-play, the teacher and classmates provide feedback on pronunciation, vocabulary use, fluency, and creativity. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the task.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To talk about learning activities in the classroom and learning with technology in the classroom in English through a matching and fill-in-the-blanks activity by using target vocabulary. Activity 1: Match & Complete The teacher provides a worksheet to the students. In the first section, students match pictures with the corresponding vocabulary words. For example, a picture of a laptop is matched with the word ''laptop''. In the second section, after understanding the meanings of the words, students complete a fill-in-the-blanks activity using a word bank (assignments, pair work, role-play, laptop, password, brainstorming, interactive activity, printer). Example sentences may include: ''Our teacher gave us three to complete by next week'', or ''Can I use the to print my report?''. At the end of the activity, the teacher checks the answers with the class, explains the correct options, and provides constructive feedback. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the task.
